newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - April regrade at minus 30cts.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - April regrade at minus 30cts.

text.p: Singapore jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade traded late afternoon on Thursday at minus 30 cents on fears that the large prompt physical negative regrade would be extended to April, traders said.
"There are some talks that the support for the gas oil market will be extended to April," one trader said.
April regrade was last quoted at minus 35 to minus 25 cents per barrel, brokers said.

As a result of the current support for the prompt physical gas oil the physical regrade has widened to more than $1.00 per barrel but many thought that the spread will collapse in April once the present support for gas oil is gone.
Gas oil prices have risen by more than $3.00 per barrel since early March due to the large purchases of local trader Hin Leong who had bought more than 5.7 million barrels over the period.
In the physical market, jet fuel continued to slide with an April 18-22 cargo offered at $26.30, down 50 cents from Tuesday.
The gas oil swaps rebounded slightly with April last quoted at $25.90/$26.00 per barrel down from Wednesday's $25.35/$25.40, brokers said.
The market traded earlier in the day at $26.00 and 25.98 while May traded at $25.07 and $25.00.

Traders said the market lost some ground due to the selling onslaught seen late Wednesday when seven offers to sell physical cargoes emerged at between $27.20 and $28.50, down from Tuesday's traded levels of $28.20 for early April and $29.00 for second half April.
Also players felt that local trader Hin Leong might be nearing the end of his buying spree which has already totalled around 5.7 million barrels.
Fuel oil swaps were largely unchanged in quiet trading but the April/May spread widened to value at about 50 cents per tonne from about 25 cents early Wednesday.
April was quoted at $99.00/$99.75 and May at $98.00/$98.75, brokers said.
